trust_decision.summary: Option values are trusted to be bare numbers and written straight into SVG markup: every attribute in @dicebear/core and in the style packages is XML-escaped except the rotate transform in @dicebear/core and the font-size/font-weight attributes in @dicebear/initials, which interpolate the raw option value.

landing_point.why: The advisory headline names the unescaped rotate option in @dicebear/core, and addRotate is the only place that option is concatenated into markup; it is also the first hunk of the published fix.

fix_sites.entry_point: createAvatar(style, options) exported by @dicebear/core (packages/@dicebear/core/src/core.ts:8; rotate is handed to addRotate at core.ts:46); result.toString()/toJson()/toDataUri() then emit the string

create exported by @dicebear/initials (packages/@dicebear/initials/src/index.ts:24), invoked through createAvatar with the initials Style and re-exported by @dicebear/collection (packages/@dicebear/collection/src/index.ts:17)
fix_sites.module_kind: style package, second implementation with its own duplicated escape helper (packages/@dicebear/initials/src/utils/escape.ts:1)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The initials style is a separate package with its own escapeXml helper already applied to font-family, fill and the initials text, and its options are typed as numbers and bounded by its JSON schema, so the style body looks type-safe and out of the core advisory's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Numeric options must keep rendering as bare numbers (rotate 90/120 must stay 'rotate(90,' and fontSize 42 must stay 'font-size="42"'); escape.xml/escapeXml only accept a string, so a fix that passes the number itself (or Number()/parseInt() coercion) either throws a TypeError on the default numeric path or silently turns values into NaN, and the existing whole-output fixtures pin the exact bytes.

O6_input_shapes: number: integer default and explicit value (rotate: 90, fontSize: 42, fontWeight: 400) which must be stringified, not rejected
fractional or negative number (rotate: 22.5, negative translate values)
array: survives the JSON round-trip in options merge and is comma-joined by the template literal, so an array of strings also reaches the sink
object: stringified as [object Object] by the template literal rather than reaching String.prototype

O8b_injection_room.sibling: gradientTransform="rotate(${rotation} 0.5 0.5)" in addBackground uses the same numeric-into-transform mechanism as addRotate.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same file, same author and the same shape of code; it is only safe because the value happens to come from prng.integer rather than from options.backgroundRotation, which a maintainer could plausibly have interpolated instead.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: scale(${scale / 100}) and translate(${translateX} ${translateY}) in addScale/addTranslate interpolate the scale/translate options into a transform attribute.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: These are the sibling per-option transform helpers; they are safe only because the arithmetic numifies the option, and a refactor that emits the raw option (as addRotate does) would reproduce the hole.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: dy="${(fontSize * .356).toFixed(3)}" and any new numeric text option (letter-spacing, stroke-width) emitted on the same <text> element.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same attribute row, same option; it escapes notice because the arithmetic coercion hides the missing escape, so a maintainer adding one more numeric attribute would copy the unescaped pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: rotate(${this.rotation ?? 0} ...) with translate(${this.offsetX ?? 0}, ${this.offsetY ?? 0}) inside a transform attribute; the same code is duplicated in packages/@dicebear/glass/src/utils/pickComponent.ts:66, packages/@dicebear/rings/src/utils/pickComponent.ts:66 and packages/@dicebear/thumbs/src/utils/pickComponent.ts:66.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The rotation/offset inputs are the option arrays (shape1Rotation, ringRotation, faceRotation ...) and are only numified later by prng.integer, so a maintainer feeding the option array straight into the transform would create the same sink in four packages.

O9_family: improper neutralization of user-controlled option values in generated SVG markup (SVG/HTML injection leading to script execution in a browser; advisory tags CWE-79 and CWE-184)

O10_build.toolchain: npm workspaces (npm@11.6.2) driven by turbo, per-package `tsc` build to lib/, `node --test` runner, node >= 18
O10_build.project_tests: Per-package whole-output snapshot tests: packages/@dicebear/core/tests/create.test.js and packages/@dicebear/initials/tests/create.test.js compare createAvatar(...).toString() and toJson() against packages/@dicebear/*/tests/static/create/*.svg|json (core fixtures include rotate: 90 and rotate: 120; initials fixtures include fontSize: 90 and fontSize: 50). Unit tests for both escape helpers: packages/@dicebear/core/tests/utils/escape.test.js and packages/@dicebear/initials/tests/utils/escape.test.js. The security.test.js files the fix adds are absent from the pinned tree.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Escape only the rotate value where the report's payload reproduces (addRotate, with escape.xml(rotate) or a Number()/parseInt() coercion) and stop, leaving the font-size/font-weight sinks of the initials style and the non-string input shapes untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/@dicebear/initials/src/index.ts:38 also emits dy from (fontSize * .356).toFixed(3); it is safe only because the arithmetic numifies the option, same mechanism but no injection - not pursued.

packages/@dicebear/converter/src/utils/svg.ts:8-18 reparses and rebuilds the whole SVG with fast-xml-parser using processEntities: false, a save/reload boundary for the same markup; whether entities survive that round trip unchanged is outside this advisory's fix and was not pursued.

apps/docs/.vitepress/theme/utils/escape.ts:1 carries a third escaping implementation (escapeHtml/escapeJsString/escapeShellArg) for generated code snippets; same duplication smell, different sink, not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb: no directory-size tooling was available (read/search only), so the tiny_repo (<5 MB) and giant_repo (>1.5 GB) thresholds could not be assessed.

CLI reachability: read but not executed - packages/dicebear/src/utils/validateInputBySchema.ts:9 validates options with Ajv (coerceTypes, removeAdditional) against the core and style schemas, so rotate/fontSize strings are rejected there and the CLI is not counted as an O1 entry point; if Ajv coerced a payload through, the CLI would be a third entry point.

The editor and docs playgrounds pass URL/UI options into createAvatar in the browser and render the SVG through a data: URI in an ; whether any of their render paths could execute the injected markup was not assessed (not executed).

Scope-trap strength: the supplied advisory summary itself names '@dicebear/initials fontSize/fontWeight' next to core's rotate, so if the solver-facing report keeps that wording the O2 second-implementation site is described rather than discoverable.
